chunks: From him, from al-Sayyārī, from Muḥammad ibn Aslam, from a man from the people of al-Jazīrah, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Should one perform salat over the buried person after he has been buried?” He said: “No. If it were permissible for anyone, it would have been permissible for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Rather, salat is not performed over the buried person after he has been buried, nor over the naked person.”

So the proper way regarding these reports is one of two possibilities. One of them is what our Shaykh used to hold, and that is that salat over the grave is only permissible for a day and a night, no more than that. Thus, whatever has been reported concerning the permissibility of salat over him after burial, he interpreted as referring to that day; and whatever has been reported that it is not permissible, he interpreted as referring to what is after that day.
And the second possibility is that what is meant by the permissibility of salat over the buried person is supplication for him, apart from the prescribed salat; and that indicates this.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ الْمُرَتَّبَةِ: the prescribed formal salat, distinguished from mere supplication
key_terms.الْعُرْيَانِ: the naked person, mentioned here as one over whom salat is not performed
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave, as the location discussed for post-burial prayer
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: to perform salat, here referring to funeral salat

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform funeral salat over a person after they have already been buried?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of performing salat over a deceased person after burial and presents a clear denial from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام. It then offers two ways to reconcile differing reports: either limiting permissibility to within a day and night after burial, or understanding such reports as referring to du'a for the deceased rather than the formal funeral salat.
